To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the changes in terrigenous and marine productivity in the southeastern Brazilian continental shelf are controlled by the changes in the Intetropical Convergence Zone, and that the changes in the marine productivity are strongly controlled by changes on the terrigenous input.
the terrigenous input and the marine primary productivity were strongly controlled by the changes in the Intetropical Convergence Zone.
the terrigenous input, marine productivity and the climate of the South Atlantic Ocean are strongly controlled by changes on the ITCZ and winds associated with SACCZ.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the reconstruction of the paleoenvironmental conditions of the southeastern Brazilian margin and the adjacent ocean during the last glacial-interglacial cycle.
the relationship between continental climate and marine productivity in SE Brazil, which is important to understand the paleoceanographic conditions and the paleoclimate of the South Atlantic Ocean.
the study of changes in marine productivity and terrigenous input during the MIS 5, which is the last interglacial-glacial cycle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the changes in marine primary productivity were controlled by changes in terrigenous flux, which in turn were controlled by changes on precipitation over the southeastern Brazilian continent.

the terrigenous input and primary productivity were strongly controlled by changes on the Intertropical and Subtropical Convergence Zones, as well as by the wind regime associated with the South Equatorial Current, the South Atlantic Convergent Zone and the Brazil Current.

during sub-stages MIS 5d and MIS 5b, both precipitation rate over the continent and marine primary productivity were higher than the present ones, while during the other sub-stages, MIS 5c and MIS 5e, both were lower than present.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

changes in terrigenous and marine productivity in the southeastern Brazilian margin are controlled by changes in precipitation rate over SE Brazil and changes in marine primary productivity in the South Brazil Bight, which would have been controlled by changes in wind regimes associated with the ITCZ and SACZ.
changes in terrigenous fluxes and calcareous nannabinofossils assemblages are a reliable record of the paleoclimate of the SE Brazil and the South Atlantic Ocean, respectively.
changes in terrigenous inputs and marine primary productivity were controlled by changes in wind regimes and the Intertropical and South Atlantic Convergence Zones.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the calcareous nannofoossil assemblages are a good indicator of marine productivity, which is strongly influenced by terrigenous input, and therefore, by changes in precipitation over the southeastern Brazilian margin.
the calcareous nammofossil assemblage is an effective proxy to infer changes in marine productivity in the SE Brazilian margin.

the terrigenous input and the calcareous nanno-fossil assemblage variations in the South Atlantic can be used to estimate the paleo-precipitation and paleo-productivity rates, respectively, for the South American continent and for the South Atlantic Ocean, respectively.
